description: Read from any viaSocket API endpoint with a GET request for the user and return its response. Use it once you know the exact endpoint: look it up with get_viasocket_api_docs first to get its URL, headers, query params and body, unless the skill or a dedicated tool on this server already gives them exactly. Load the quickstart-viasocket skill first: it explains which tool to use when. For POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE use call_any_api_of_viasocket. Pass the full url with path variables filled in, the headers the docs list, and query params in `query` (not in the url). For the auth header the docs name (Authorization, proxy_auth_token, x-api-key, ...), pass it with an empty value "": the signed-in user's token is filled in automatically. Never put a real or made-up token there; if the docs name no auth header, leave it out and the token is sent as Authorization. If the API needs the user to sign in, they're asked the first time. Returns { status, ok, headers, data }: the HTTP status and the response body, including error details on failure.

headers.description: Request headers as name/value pairs, as the docs list them. Give the auth header (Authorization, proxy_auth_token, x-api-key, ...) an empty value "" so the signed-in user's token is filled in; never put a token here yourself. Pass {} when the endpoint needs no headers. Example: {"proxy_auth_token": "", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

query.description: Query params as name/value pairs; an array sends the param once per item. Example: {"type": "flow", "bringflows": true}

url.description: Full endpoint URL with path variables replaced by real values, e.g. https://api.example.com/users/42. Put query params in `query`, not here.

name: call_any_read_api_of_viasocket
